full_judgment:
2. The facts relevant to dispose of the appeal, in short, are that the appellant as plaintiff instituted the original suit being No. 101 of 2000 in the Court of Assistant Judge Chowddagram, Cumilla for declaration of title and khas possession, alleging, inter alia, that one Abdul Gazi was the original owner of the suit land. During Chakla Roshnabad settlement operation, the CR Khatian was recorded in his name. Abdul Gazi died leaving behind four sons as his heirs, namely, Wazuddin, Miazan, Abdul and Alimuddin. By amicable arrangement, Alimuddin and Abdul got the land of first schedule and while owning and possessing 14 decimals land of the suit plot, Alimuddin died leaving behind four sons, namely, Tajul Islam, Saku Mia, Bazlur Rahman and Ibrahim and one daughter, Asia Khatun. At the time of SA operation, Khatian No. 106 was prepared in their names. By amicable arrangement, Saku Mia got 4 decimals land from the suit plot and he died leaving behind one daughter, namely, Bachuni Bibi, by his first wife and two sons (plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2) and two daughters named Amena and Tafura, by his second wife, Jobeda Begum. After that, Jobeda died leaving behind two daughters and two sons (plaintiff, Nos. 1 and 2). Among the heirs, the plaintiffs got the suit land by amicable partition and built shops on the suit land and have been possessing the same through tenants. Accordingly, the plaintiffs got their names recorded in 4 decimals land (3 decimals from plot No. 591 and 1 decimal from plot No. 597). Defendant No. 2 sold ½ decimal land to Safu Mia, son of Sekander Ali by a registered deed of sale dated 18-1-1982. The plaintiffs' suit land is on the northern side of the land sold by defendant No. 2. Defendant No. 1 sold ½ decimal land to Bhola Mia, son of Hosson Ali by a registered deed of sale dated 6-3-1989. The plaintiffs filed a suit for permanent injunction against the defendants who having been infuriated by the Filing of the suit dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land. Hence, this suit-has been filed. 

 14. The plaintiff-appellant has come with an allegation that aforesaid Alimuddin and Abdul acquired 0.28 acre land from CR Khatian No. 9 by way of amicable arrangement among the co-sharers. It has been further alleged that said Alimuddin as owner in possession over 0.14 acre land died leaving behind Tour sons in Tazul Islam, Soku Mia, Bazlur Rahman and Ibrahim and one daughter in Asia Khatun. It has been further alleged that Soku Mia alone acquired 0.04 acre land by way of amicable arrangement among the brother and sister and thereafter Soku Mia died leaving behind one daughter in Bechuni Bibi by his 1st wife and two sons, plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and two daughters in Amina Begum and Tafura Begum by his second wife Jobaida who subsequently died leaving behind two sons (plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and one daughter in Tafura). It has been also alleged that the plaintiff Nos. l and 2 acquired entire 0.04 acre land which have been recorded under plot No. 430 by way of amicable arrangement among the co-sharer and they constructed a homestead and shops therein and thereafter have been possessing the same by engaging Abul Kasham Dealer, Dr. Nazir Ahamed and Probir Mistry as monthly tenant. It has been further alleged that during RS operation 0.03 acre land has been recorded under plot No. 599 and 0.01 acre has been recorded in plot No. 597. It has been further alleged that defendant No. 2, Abdul Awal, transferred 0.05 decimal land to one Soku Mia son of Sekandar Ali by a Kabala dated 18-1-1982 and defendant No. 1 sold other 0.05 decimal land to one Bhola Mia son of Hossain Ali by a Kabala dated 6-3-1989 but all of a sudden defendant Nos. l and 2 threatened the plaintiff with dispossession from 0.03 acre of land under plot number 599 and, as such, plaintiffs were compelled to institute a suit being No. 80 of 2000 for permanent injunction, but on receiving the summons of that case, the defendants dispossessed the plaintiff from that land and building by ousting their varatia. Thereafter it has been alleged that the appellant plaintiff requested the defendant to quit the aforesaid land and building in their favour but they denied it and, as such, the plaintiff-appellants were compelled institute the present suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession after withdrawing the suit for permanent injunction. 

 19. In the instant case, the plaintiff-appellant at first instituted a suit for permanent injunction and alleging that during pendency of that suit the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs and, as such, the plaintiff has instituted the present suit seeking declaration of title and recovery of khas possession after withdrawing the previous suit for permanent injunction. Although the contesting defendants are not stranger but they indulged some strangers to enter into the suit jote and at last the defendants claimed only 0.01 acre of land from the suit jote. 

 27. Because of subsequent dispossession, the appellants did not proceed with the suit for permanent injunction filed by them and again filed the present suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession and the High Court Division erroneously held that the suit is not maintainable because of dismissal of the suit for permanent injunction and disbelieved the plaintiffs' previous possession and thus passed the impugned judgment which is required to be interfered with by this Division.
